events_detected.title: US-Iran DIRECT STATE-ON-STATE EXCHANGE: Iran missiles at two US bases in Jordan; supertanker mined in Hormuz; US weighing Kharg Island strike
events_detected.description: Escalation stack 00:15Z Sep 1: (1) Iran launched missile attack on TWO US bases in Jordan Sunday night - retaliation for US Larak Island strike; all but one missile intercepted, Trump says US let one pass as it wasn't going to hit anything. (2) Trump Monday: 'We're going to hit them hard. There will be a response.' Also: could still 'smack' Iran 'to see what happens'. (3) Fox live update: US weighing retaliation on KHARG ISLAND - Iran's primary crude export terminal; strike would remove Iran's oil lifeline and trigger global energy shock. (4) Iranian state media: supertanker caught fire/disabled in southern Hormuz after striking two naval mines (Iran frames vessels as violating passage rules). (5) CENTCOM wave of strikes on Iranian command centres, air defence, missile/drone capabilities, coastal surveillance near strait; disabled unladen tanker heading to Iranian port. (6) Hormuz commercial transit remains effectively closed Day ~185. (7) US Treasury reimposed oil-export sanctions lifted under Islamabad Memorandum.

events_detected.title: September dual-tightening convergence: Fed hike odds 58%, Bessent $4B buybacks Sep 9, JGB 2Y 31-yr high, yen >160
events_detected.description: Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole lifted Sept hike odds to 58% from 35%; markets read him as endorsing a hike while not all FOMC convinced. Bessent long-end buyback cap doubles to $4B/operation effective Sept 9 - direct Treasury-Fed conflict (Warsh wants quieter Fed, less Treasury in markets). Japan: JGB 2Y 1.70% 31-year high; 10Y 2.95% 30-year high; yen breached 160 post-Jackson Hole; BOJ deputy gov signalled no clear hike timing (brief yields retreat); failed US-Japan joint intervention backdrop. Dual Fed+BOJ tightening September = carry trade unwind risk intact.

events_detected.title: France 'poster child' of eurozone debt problems: 10Y OAT 4.1% highest since 2010, borrowing costs near 2008 highs
events_detected.description: CNBC Aug 31: France becoming 'poster child' of sovereign debt problems; growth expectations revised lower, debt ratio set to keep rising, yields at levels not seen since the financial crisis, spending restraint politically impossible pre-presidential election. AEI: 10Y French yield 4.1%, highest since 2010. OAT-Bund spreads widening; analysis consensus: French problem not yet full eurozone crisis, but France too large for ECB to ignore if spread widens further.

events_detected.title: Ebola PHEIC split: Uganda outbreak declared OVER by WHO; DRC continues exponential expansion (2,715 deaths)
events_detected.description: WHO declared Uganda's Ebola outbreak over Aug 26 (Al Jazeera). DRC outbreak continues expanding exponentially 'in an area the size of France' (2026 Ebola epidemic wiki, updated Aug 31); 2,715 deaths per ECDC-cited government data; Ituri province epicentre. Net change vs prior scan: slight de-escalation (Uganda clear) but core DRC epidemic uncontained.

events_detected.title: Market complacency divergence: VIX <15 with Hormuz closed + direct US-Iran missile exchange + 58% hike odds
events_detected.description: Observational risk flag: S&P/Dow/Nasdaq slipped Monday but capped a winning August; VIX below 15 (Santoli), 'remains below 20' per technicals. Historical pattern: VIX seasonally climbs into September. Markets are NOT pricing Hormuz closure, US-Iran missile exchanges, or dual CB tightening - complacency into the September pivot month sets up gap-risk on the snap.
